why: The FTW is a particular seven-session workshop sequence with fixed sessions, timing, participant numbers, facilitators, and a specific technology-design goal, so it is a study-specific design rather than a general canonical pattern.
The FTW toolkit is a named, downloadable package for implementing a specific seven-session participatory design workshop method rather than a general instructional element.
name: FTW toolkit for running Future Technology Workshops
product_description: A workshop implementation package that provides the structure, materials, and session instructions for running Future Technology Workshops, enabling facilitators to conduct participatory design with children or adults without specialist software-design training.

why: This is a laboratory flip-teaching implementation explicitly organized around Merrill's First Principles of Instruction, so its design and evidence belong on that canonical page rather than constituting a new theory.
The FTF-K is a named concentration assessment instrument used to measure children's attention, not a reusable instructional element.
name: FTF-K Attention Test for Children of Age 5-6 (Frankfurter Tests für Fünfjährige-Konzentration)
product_description: A timed visual-search concentration test developed by Raatz and Möhling in which young children mark target pears among distractor apples.
